Cohen's f Effect Size

Source: R/cohen_f.R
cohen_f.Rd

Computes Cohen's f, the standard deviation of the group means divided by the standard deviation within the groups, from one of three complete specifications: the group means with the within-group variance (and the group sizes, when the groups differ in size), eta squared, or the two standard deviations.

Usage

cohen_f(
  means = NULL,
  var_within = NULL,
  n_per_group = NULL,
  eta_squared = NULL,
  sd_means = NULL,
  sd_within = NULL
)

Arguments

means

Numeric vector of group means, one per group and at least two: population means for the population f, or observed sample means for the plug-in value. Give with var_within.

var_within

The within-group variance, a single positive number: the population variance common to the groups, or, for the plug-in value, the pooled within-group mean square (the mean square error of the one-way analysis of variance). Give with means.

n_per_group

Optional, and used only with means: the group sizes, one per group, which weight each group mean by its share of the total, \(n_j / N\). A single number states equal groups and gives the same result as NULL, the default, which weights the means equally (\(1 / k\) each, for k groups).

eta_squared

Eta squared, the proportion of the variance that the groups account for, a single number in [0, 1). Give it alone. A population value gives the population f. A sample eta squared gives the plug-in value \(\sqrt{df_1 F / df_2}\), which is larger than the value from the observed means and the pooled mean square (see Details).

sd_means

The standard deviation of the group means, \(\sigma_m\), a single number of at least 0, computed with divisor k (or with the weights \(n_j / N\)), not with the divisor k - 1 that stats::sd() uses. Give with sd_within.

sd_within

The within-group standard deviation, \(\sigma\), a single positive number, or, for the plug-in value, the square root of the pooled within-group mean square. Give with sd_means.

Value

A one-row data.frame (printed through dmar_tbl) with columns term and value; term is "cohen_f" and value is f at full precision.

Details

Cohen's f is defined with population quantities (Cohen, 1988, p. 276): \(f = \sigma_m / \sigma\), where \(\sigma_m\) is the standard deviation of the population means and \(\sigma\) is the standard deviation within the populations. Given population values, the function returns the population f. Given sample summaries, it returns the plug-in value from the same calculation. The plug-in value depends on which summaries are given: from the same data, a sample eta squared gives a larger value than the observed group means with the pooled within-group mean square (see below). Sample inputs do not make the result an unbiased estimate of the population f: the spread of sample means includes their sampling error as well as the spread of the population means. Unequal group sizes determine how the group means are weighted; without n_per_group the means are weighted equally.

A call gives exactly one complete specification: means with var_within (and n_per_group if wanted), eta_squared alone, or sd_means with sd_within. Each determines f on its own, so an argument of one specification given with an argument of another is refused, as is one half of a pair given alone, or n_per_group without means; the refusal has class dmar_argument_invalid.

From the means, with weights \(w_j = 1 / k\) by default or \(w_j = n_j / N\) when n_per_group is given, $$\bar\mu = \sum_j w_j \mu_j, \qquad \sigma_m^2 = \sum_j w_j (\mu_j - \bar\mu)^2, \qquad f = \sqrt{\sigma_m^2 / \sigma^2}.$$ The divisor of \(\sigma_m^2\) is k (or N), because the variance is that of a fixed set of means. From eta squared, \(f = \sqrt{\eta^2 / (1 - \eta^2)}\) (Kim, 2016, p. 233), and from the two standard deviations, \(f = \sigma_m / \sigma\). Given population values for the same populations, with the same weighting of the means, the three give the same f.

Given sample summaries, the three agree only when the within-group variance is defined the same way in each. With the observed means, the group sizes, and the pooled within-group mean square, \(SS_{within} / (N - k)\), of a one-way design, \(N \sigma_m^2\) is the between-groups sum of squares, so the plug-in value equals \(\sqrt{df_1 F / N}\), with F, \(df_1 = k - 1\), and \(df_2 = N - k\) from the analysis of variance. A sample eta squared, \(SS_{between} / SS_{total}\), pairs with the within-group variance \(SS_{within} / N\) rather than with the mean square, so the value from it, \(\sqrt{SS_{between} / SS_{within}}\) \(= \sqrt{df_1 F / df_2}\), is larger than the value from the means and the pooled mean square by the factor \(\sqrt{N / (N - k)}\). The two are equal when var_within is \(SS_{within} / N\) (or sd_within is its square root). Without n_per_group, the means of unequal groups are weighted equally and the value differs from both. The square root of the signal-to-noise ratio of ci_srsnr is this f with the weights \(n_j / N\) and the pooled mean square; that function gives its confidence interval from F or from the same summaries.

References

Cohen, J. (1988). Statistical power analysis for the behavioral sciences (2nd ed.). Hillsdale, NJ: Lawrence Erlbaum.

Kim, H.-Y. (2016). Statistical notes for clinical researchers: Sample size calculation 3. Comparison of several means using one-way ANOVA. Restorative Dentistry & Endodontics, 41(3), 231–234. doi:10.5395/rde.2016.41.3.231

See also

ci_srsnr, ci_snr, ss_power_one_way_anova, ss_power_R2

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# Kim (2016, Table 1) plans a four-group study around means of 18.4,
# 22.2, 25.1, and 32.1 with a common standard deviation of 8.6, and
# reports f as .58. At full precision, this f plans a balanced study of
# 40, ten per group, for power .80 at the .05 level, as the article does.
f_kim <- cohen_f(means = c(18.4, 22.2, 25.1, 32.1), var_within = 8.6^2)
f_kim
#>  term    value
#>  cohen_f 0.583
ss_power_one_way_anova(a = 4, true_f = f_kim$value, desired_power = .80)
#>  term              value 
#>  necessary_N       40    
#>  n_per_group       10    
#>  a                 4     
#>  noncentral_f_parm 13.603
#>  actual_power      0.847 

# Cohen (1988, p. 277) places seven population means over half a
# within-population standard deviation, one at each end and five at the
# midpoint, and gives f as .13 (.267 times .5, his Equation 8.2.8).
cohen_f(means = c(-.25, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, .25), var_within = 1)
#>  term    value
#>  cohen_f 0.134

# The plug-in value from the summaries of an observed one-way design
# with unequal groups: the group means, the pooled within-group mean
# square, and the group sizes of the three arms of drinks_trial.
fit <- stats::lm(log_drinks ~ treatment, data = drinks_trial)
cohen_f(means = tapply(drinks_trial$log_drinks, drinks_trial$treatment, mean),
        var_within = sum(stats::residuals(fit)^2) / stats::df.residual(fit),
        n_per_group = as.vector(table(drinks_trial$treatment)))
#>  term    value
#>  cohen_f 0.311

# The sample eta squared of the same fit gives a larger plug-in value,
# by the factor sqrt(N / (N - k)) = sqrt(88 / 85) (see Details).
ss <- stats::anova(fit)[["Sum Sq"]]
cohen_f(eta_squared = ss[1] / sum(ss))
#>  term    value
#>  cohen_f 0.317

# From eta squared, and from the two standard deviations:
cohen_f(eta_squared = .10)
#>  term    value
#>  cohen_f 0.333
cohen_f(sd_means = 4, sd_within = 8)
#>  term    value
#>  cohen_f 0.500
